g241v7i3pd0nca912jcj2ius20: Where a world lives: a Clifford algebra (made once from its signature, the squares of its basis vectors, and its basis), the unit vectors along the box's axes, which way is down, which vector points away from the viewer (none in a flat world), the rotor that turns the world to face the camera, and how large one unit is drawn, as a share of the picture.
emg1sii971f68d3inpeqfgcse6: A rigid body: where its centre is and how fast it moves (vectors), how it is turned (a rotor) and how fast it turns (a bivector, the plane it spins in, as long as its rate), the radius it bounces at, and its shape: corners around its centre and the edges between them, by number.
dgr8n38p5sck3k4akcdkiof76i: a · b, the geometric product of the space's algebra.
2aa7i6oj7hqc1vrhbbc2mm9rfl: The body a moment dt later: gravity pulls its velocity down, the air takes 10% of its velocity and 60% of its spin each second, it moves along its velocity, and it turns by the rotor e^(−dt/2 · spin), which goes in front of the rotor it had.
4ahl9mq7mmrormffqubf1vt21p: A body rubbing on what it touches, at the point r from its centre. That point moves at v + ½(rΩ − Ωr): the body's velocity plus how its spin Ω carries the point round. The part of that along the surface is the slip. Friction pushes against the slip, on the body's velocity and, through the bivector r ∧ push, on its spin, taking off 50% of the slip each frame, so a spinning body starts to roll and a sliding one starts to turn. A body turns as if its mass were spread like a disc's (I = ½ m r²), so the push is a third of the slip. Rolling also loses 3% of the spin each frame it touches, so a rolling body comes to rest.
rhdl5grmj7atka6pkbhivl709o: The body after the walls, one axis of the box at a time. A body past a wall is put back against it. If it is still moving out, the part of its velocity across the wall (clifford project onto the axis) turns round and keeps 70% of its speed, and it rubs on the wall where it touches it. With no loss and no rubbing this would be a reflection in the wall.
bhtvsi7l5odbc1nh507ngfkrr4: Two bodies after they meet. Overlapping bodies are pushed apart along the line between their centres until they just touch. If they are closing in, the part of their closing velocity along that line (clifford project onto it) is shared out so they part at 70% of the speed they met at (Newton's law of restitution). Equal masses.
b166cpbkmrh8sjmn8d90he9i0n: A body and the others after it has met each of them in turn.
at27po7ht781up91jml2s496jj: Every pair of bodies, met once.
46bqbcs5ps5pgj0eba8rusjtn8: The world one frame (1/60 s) later. The same definition moves the flat world and the solid one: only the space it is given differs.
